stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is mapping out what a proposed collaborative practice agreement could cover. Which activities may fall within collaborative drug therapy management as the statute defines it? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Initiating, monitoring, modifying and discontinuing the patient's drug therapy.
Collecting and reviewing the patient's history.
Obtaining and checking pulse, temperature, blood pressure and respiration.
Settling a diagnosis where a laboratory result plainly supports one.
Ordering and evaluating laboratory tests directly related to the drug therapy.

explanation.core_reasoning: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(a) defines collaborative drug therapy management as the initiating, monitoring, modifying and discontinuing of a patient's drug therapy under an agreement, and provides that it may include collecting and reviewing histories, obtaining and checking the named vital signs, and ordering and evaluating laboratory tests directly related to drug therapy on the stated conditions.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: this is the core of the defined activity.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: the four named vital signs are expressly included.
choice_analysis.D: The evaluation shall not include a diagnostic component.
choice_analysis.E: Correct, subject to physician supervision or direct consultation and an approved protocol.

related_facts: Laboratory work requires an approved protocol applicable to the practice setting
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates assume that a pharmacist who may order and evaluate a test may also act on what it shows.

reasoning_steps: Exclude anything that amounts to a diagnostic conclusion
